newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB shares gain ground but future uncertain.
newsitem.headline: NCB shares gain ground but future uncertain.

text.p: Shares of Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) may manage a near-term comeback on short-covering but their future remains uncertain, several analysts said on Thursday.
They warned that NCB stocks should be avoided as a long-term investment since the bank is in one of the weakest financial positions of the nation"s top 20 banks.

In Thursday"s afternoon trading, NCB shares traded at 238 yen, up 34 yen or 16.67 percent, making it the largest percentage gainer on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Volume was also the heaviest on the first section.

Thursday"s gains were sparked by comments on Wednesday by a senior official of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), who said public money could be used to protect creditors holding bank debentures, brokers said.
"In the short-term, short-covering is expected to push up NCB shares," said Akira Takai, an analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd.

But after a round of short covering, the shares may stay flat as the market is likely to wait for the bank"s business results for fiscal 1996/97 ending March 31 in order to reassess the bank"s financial health, he said.
Fiorillo said NCB was technically insolvent if it was assumed the bank would bear the burden of all of its lending exposure to its non-bank affiliates, estimated at 225 billion yen.

"Yet banks that are technically insolvent from a Western investment accounting point of view are allowed to continue to operate in Japan if the authorities deem it an operation that can be turned around," he said.

NCB"s senior managing director Tadao Iwaki told Reuters in an interview last week that the bank had no liquidity problems, adding that although it has restrained debenture issues, it still had ample funds worth one trillion yen and securities worth some three trillion yen.
